title: Kubernetes Audit Log Baseline

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay or inject sample `kube:audit` events matching `*` into `index=kube`. Confirm UC-4.9.1 search returns >=1 row and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `kube:audit` traffic without `*` markers. Confirm the search returns zero rows and alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=kube` sourcetype=`kube:audit` collected via Splunk Connect for Kubernetes (Splunkbase 4467); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=kube sourcetype="kube:audit"
| table _time user.username verb objectRef.resource objectRef.name
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.9.1_kubernetes_audit_log_bas_1"
| sort -_time
description: Verifies kubernetes audit log baseline data flows into Splunk continuously. This UC monitors `kube:audit` for kubernetes audit log baseline and surfaces events for SOC triage, change review, and compliance evidence.
value: Kubernetes Audit Log Baseline is the prerequisite feed for all 4.9 detections. Detecting kubernetes audit log baseline early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable kube:audit ingestion via the appropriate Splunk TA into index=kube.
visualization: Ingestion health single value and lag chart.
knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=kube`.
• Install and configure Splunk Connect for Kubernetes (Splunkbase 4467) with the modular input for `kube:audit`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): none.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `user.username` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable kube:audit ingestion via the appropriate Splunk TA into index=kube.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=kube sourcetype="kube:audit" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=kube sourcetype="kube:audit"
| table _time user.username verb objectRef.resource objectRef.name
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.9.1_kubernetes_audit_log_bas_1"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `kube:audit` in `index=kube` to detect kubernetes audit log baseline. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Kubernetes audit dashboard for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `user.username` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_9_1_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Ingestion health single value and lag chart..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Connect for Kubernetes (Splunkbase 4467) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of kubernetes audit log baseline so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
